git.dirty_describes: 'dirty' here = uncommitted TRACKED modifications in the SOURCE WORKTREE at capture time. It says nothing about whether the measured binary was built from a clean tree; that is identity.binary_provenance.dirty.
git.note: SOURCE WORKTREE HEAD at the moment this artifact was written. It does NOT describe the binary that was measured -- the tool's worktree and the worktree that compiled the exe are frequently different lanes. For the commit that was actually exercised, read identity.binary_provenance.

binary_provenance.dirty_describes: uncommitted TRACKED modifications in the worktree the BINARY was compiled from, at compile time
binary_provenance.note: Read out of the binary's own compiled-in build fingerprint (.rdata string literals stamped by cmake/GenerateBuildFingerprint.cmake). This is the only commit in this manifest that describes the code that ran.
